name: markdown-frontend-open-points
body:
Open design points for the plan/user, reconciled against the rules since pinned. The markdown FQN scheme, the link anchoring/target rule, the document-root section, and the root-directory module identity are now DECIDED in the durable spec; the genuinely plan-time choices are the exact slug text-mapping, the frontend's implementation language/artifact, the hybrid-extension accept set, and the link path base.

DECIDED (pinned; no longer open here):
- FQN scheme (feedback-12; requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols, requirements.requirement.markdown-accept-extensions, domain.value.module-fqn-prefix): a markdown Module's FQN is its directory's absolute path; a markdown File's FQN is the file's absolute path with the extension retained (`docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown` stay distinct); the document-root section's FQN is `<file-fqn>.<document-root-segment>` with a fixed reserved literal (e.g. `document-root`); a heading section extends its parent section's FQN. Absolute paths are unique per file and per directory and begin with `/`, so path-derived markdown identities are disjoint from language/package-derived code module FQNs and no two files or directories alias; dot-joined directory prefixes are rejected as lossy.
- Link anchoring and target rule (feedback-13; requirements.requirement.markdown-links-as-edges, requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols, domain.entity.markdown-document): every link is anchored on a Struct section, never a File (`File` is not a legal `Uses`/`UnresolvedUse` endpoint). A link in a no-heading document or in the preamble originates from that document's document-root Struct; an unanchored whole-document link targets the target document's document-root Struct; an internal anchor resolves to the matching heading section Struct; a link that cannot resolve (an external URL, a path no scanned markdown document provides, or an unmatched fragment) becomes `UnresolvedUse` → `UnresolvedTarget` with a category (`external` for a URL, `unknown` for a dangling relative path or unmatched fragment), never a guessed FQN.
- Root-directory module identity (feedback-16; domain.value.module-fqn-prefix part (3)): the repo root is itself a directory with an absolute path, so the root markdown Module's FQN is the repo-root directory's absolute path. The earlier premise that the root offers no path to name it is wrong; the leading `/` also keeps it clear of language/package-derived module names.
- Section shape / heading forms (requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols, domain.entity.markdown-document): every document carries exactly one synthesized document-root Struct — including a heading-less or single-section document — and every heading is a Struct section nested by heading level. Whether the source spelling is ATX (`#`) or setext (underline) is parser surface syntax for the same section Struct, not an FQN- or AC-affecting choice.

DEFERRED (plan-time, not decidable from the graph):
(1) exact slug rule — narrowed. The deliverable is a deterministic heading-text → one FQN segment mapping. The scheme pins what the rule must satisfy — it maps to a single segment and never embeds the `.` separator ambiguously (delimiter-safe), and it maps duplicate headings in one file to distinct segments — but the exact text→segment mapping (case, whitespace, punctuation, unicode) and the duplicate-disambiguation form remain plan-time. No AC depends on the exact rule: the collision-freedom AC is guaranteed by the pinned absolute-path prefixes and the reserved document-root literal (same-stem files and path-alias directories differ in their absolute-path prefix; the document-root is strictly shallower than every heading regardless of slug), so it does not assert a slug outcome. A duplicate-heading fixture becomes a reasonable addition once the rule lands.
(2) frontend implementation — the md frontend's own language and artifact (a new src/mdlib standalone binary built by build.rs, vs a Node/Go script) and its JSONL emission shape.
(3) accept set — whether the md id owns only .md/.markdown or also hybrid extensions such as .mdx (JSX-embedded, arguably the JS/TS frontend's concern).
(4) link path-resolution scope — narrowed to the path base. Anchoring and target selection are pinned (above); the residual is whether relative link paths resolve file-relative or repo-root-relative, and how links to non-markdown files are treated (they cannot become `Uses` edges — `File` is not a legal `Uses` target — so they can only be unresolved). The link AC is representability-based (every link becomes a `Uses` or an `UnresolvedUse`, never dropped or guessed) and so does not depend on the base; the concrete cross-document path form is fixed when the base is pinned.
